requirements.title: IEEE_SELECTED_REAL_KIND argument restrictions
requirements.definition: At least one argument shall be present; P, R, and RADIX shall be integer scalars.

pending.IEEE_SELECTED_REAL_KIND-at-least-one-arg: Positive source controls call IEEE_SELECTED_REAL_KIND(P=6), IEEE_SELECTED_REAL_KIND(R=30), and IEEE_SELECTED_REAL_KIND(RADIX=2). Mutation omits all arguments and claims no diagnostic facet.
pending.IEEE_SELECTED_REAL_KIND-P-integer-scalar: Positive source control passes scalar integer P=6. Mutation passes a rank-one P and claims no diagnostic facet.
pending.IEEE_SELECTED_REAL_KIND-R-integer-scalar: Positive source control passes scalar integer R=30. Mutation passes a rank-one R and claims no diagnostic facet.
pending.IEEE_SELECTED_REAL_KIND-RADIX-integer-sc: Positive source control passes scalar integer RADIX=2. Mutation passes a rank-one RADIX and claims no diagnostic facet.

requirements.title: IEEE_SELECTED_REAL_KIND positive result denotes an available IEEE format kind
requirements.definition: For an available ISO/IEC/IEEE 60559 floating-point format meeting the requested precision, range, and radix, the result is a kind type parameter value for such a format.

pending.IEEE_SELECTED_REAL_KIND-available-kind-p: Guarded branch probes IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE(0.0); supported branch requests P=PRECISION(0.0), R=RANGE(0.0), RADIX=RADIX(0.0) and asserts the result is positive rather than any failure code. Mutation changes RADIX to -RADIX(0.0).
pending.IEEE_SELECTED_REAL_KIND-available-kind-m: Guarded branch uses the ieee_binary profile and requests P=6, R=30, RADIX=2; supported branch asserts a positive result and records a source-use companion that any declared real of that kind has PRECISION at least 6, RANGE at least 30, and RADIX 2. Mutation raises P beyond the profiled default precision.
pending.IEEE_SELECTED_REAL_KIND-positive-kind-su: Guarded branch uses the ieee_binary profile and a named integer constant k=IEEE_SELECTED_REAL_KIND(P=6,R=30,RADIX=2); supported branch first asserts k>0, then declares a real object with KIND=k, forms REAL(0,KIND=k), and asserts IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE(REAL(0,KIND=k)) is true because k is a kind type parameter of an ISO/IEC/IEEE 60559 floating-point format. Mutation uses a non-IEEE kind source or omits the support assertion.

requirements.title: IEEE_SELECTED_REAL_KIND failure codes describe unavailable criteria
requirements.definition: Unavailable criteria return the specified negative codes -1 through -5 according to which radix, precision, and range capabilities exist.

pending.IEEE_SELECTED_REAL_KIND-minus-1-precisio: No portable exact oracle without a processor profile proving an IEEE kind of the requested radix and range exists while every such kind lacks the requested precision. Future profiled fixtures may assert -1 for a documented capability matrix.
pending.IEEE_SELECTED_REAL_KIND-minus-2-range-mi: No portable exact oracle without a processor profile proving an IEEE kind of the requested radix and precision exists while every such kind lacks the requested range. Future profiled fixtures may assert -2 for a documented capability matrix.
pending.IEEE_SELECTED_REAL_KIND-minus-3-precisio: No portable exact oracle without a processor profile proving an IEEE kind of the requested radix exists while neither requested precision nor range is met. Future profiled fixtures may assert -3 for a documented capability matrix.
pending.IEEE_SELECTED_REAL_KIND-minus-4-no-combi: No portable exact oracle: -4 requires separate IEEE kinds satisfying precision or range individually but no single kind satisfying both, and the standard mandates no such split capability. Future profiled fixtures may assert -4 only from a documented capability matrix.
pending.IEEE_SELECTED_REAL_KIND-minus-5-radix-mi: Source-control plan calls IEEE_SELECTED_REAL_KIND(P=0,R=0,RADIX=-1) and asserts -5 because RADIX intrinsic values for real models are positive; mutation changes RADIX to RADIX(0.0) under IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE(0.0).

requirements.title: IEEE_SELECTED_REAL_KIND chooses the smallest precision and then smallest kind among ties
requirements.definition: Among multiple kind values meeting the criteria, the returned value has the smallest decimal precision, then the smallest kind value among equal-precision candidates.

pending.IEEE_SELECTED_REAL_KIND-smallest-precisi: No portable exact oracle without an enumerated processor kind matrix; the standard does not provide a portable way to list every IEEE kind and compare the returned kind against unlisted candidates. Future profiled fixtures may assert the rule from a documented matrix.
pending.IEEE_SELECTED_REAL_KIND-smallest-kind-ti: No portable exact oracle without a processor profile containing at least two IEEE kinds of equal decimal precision meeting the same criteria. Future profiled fixtures may assert the smaller kind value from a documented matrix.

accounting.rationale: Description names IEEE_SELECTED_REAL_KIND as an IEEE kind type parameter inquiry.
Argument restrictions split presence, P, R, and RADIX.
Result Value combines absent-argument defaults, absent-RADIX latitude, and available-kind criteria.
The processor is not constrained to a radix for absent RADIX.
Failure-code paragraph enumerates five capability cases.
Example paragraph is illustrative and does not override the p7 tie-selection rule.
